title: Microsoft Teams: recently used emojis and reactions sync across devices
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap and Microsoft's tenant notice support the rollout, automatic enablement and stated compliance effects, and no separate sync control was found. Minor corrections should acknowledge the existing Teams licence requirement and rate the impact consistently with a default change affecting all supported users.

claims.claim: No tenant or messaging-policy switch for recently used emoji sync is documented in either admin UI or automation.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams recently used emoji sync disable admin setting Teams PowerShell CsTeamsMessagingPolicy'. Opened teams-custom-emojis, messaging-policies-in-teams, Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration and Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy; no recent-sync UI setting or parameter found.

claims.claim: The messaging policy settings page lists no recently used emoji setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams recently used emoji sync disable admin setting Teams PowerShell CsTeamsMessagingPolicy'; read the full messaging-policies-in-teams settings list, which includes Upload custom emojis and Delete custom emojis but no recently used emoji setting.

claims.claim: The use custom emojis option in Teams admin center Messaging Settings controls custom emojis.
claims.quote: In the Teams Admin Center controls, go to Messaging Settings section and toggle the use custom emojis option, found under the Custom emojis section, on or off.

claims.claim: Upload custom emojis is a messaging policy setting controlling custom emoji creation.
claims.quote: Upload custom emojis - Set which users can create custom emojis. This setting is on by default.

claims.claim: Delete custom emojis is a messaging policy setting controlling custom emoji deletion.
claims.quote: Delete custom emojis - Set which users can delete custom emojis. This setting is off by default (except for Teams admins).

claims.claim: Impact is medium despite the stated default change affecting every Teams user on supported clients.
claims.quote: impact: "medium"; impact: Medium. Every Teams user on a supported client sees the change, but it is limited to the recently used emoji and reaction list.
claims.fix: Set impact to 'high' and replace its rationale with: 'High. Every Teams user on a supported client sees a change to the default recently used emoji and reaction list.' The assessment scale defines high as most users or a change to default behaviour; cosmetic scope is already reflected in low risk.
